Hi Emma — thanks for the clear questions. Below is a concise mapping and the operational caveats for Redwood Hosted API when a tenant is configured with a US region. I've attached a short matrix and a zipped evidence bundle for your procurement packet (custsec-greenfield-evidence.zip).

1) Residency / storage locations
- Primary storage: For tenants configured to the US region, request payloads (prompts) and generated outputs are stored in AWS us-west-2 data centers by default.
- Temporary caches: Low-latency caches (KV caches, in-memory) live on the serving fleet in the same region and are not shipped to other geographic regions during normal operation.
- Replication: We do not replicate customer request/response content to other geographic regions for routine redundancy. However, metadata required for platform health and rollout safety (non-personally-identifying runtime telemetry) may be asynchronously sent to our central control plane (hosted in us-east-1) for operational telemetry. That telemetry is pseudonymized and does not include full prompt/response payloads.

2) Backups & disaster recovery
- Persistent backups: We take backups of model-serving state and internal metadata; backups of customer payloads are not part of routine snapshot backups. In rare disaster-recovery cases we may rely on encrypted snapshots of ephemeral storage — these are retained only long enough to recover active service and are subject to our encryption and access controls (see attestation in the attachment).
- Legal hold / exports: If a legal hold is requested, separate preservation workflows are used and require a signed request by an authorized Greenfield contact.

3) Retention and deletion timelines
- Default data retention (hosted API): By default, request/response payloads are retained for 30 days to support abuse detection, troubleshooting, and model quality monitoring.
- Deletion on request: We honor customer deletion requests. For hosted API customers, data deletion from active stores is typically completed within 72 hours of a verified request.
- Backups & caches: Deletion from backup artifacts can take longer due to snapshot/recovery windows; we aim to purge customer payloads from backups within 90 days, with a best-effort target of 30 days depending on snapshot cadence.
- Billing & audit logs: Billing usage metrics and minimal billing identifiers are retained for 13 months for invoicing and compliance. Audit logs required for security investigations may be retained up to 24 months, and will not contain full customer payloads.

4) Hard wipe / account termination
- On account termination we initiate a complete deletion workflow which includes active stores, caches, and scheduled retention for backups. We provide a deletion certificate once the workflow completes. If Greenfield requires a shorter backup purge SLA or on-prem evidence, recommend Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) for contractual residency guarantees and shorter deletion guarantees.

Attachments included:
- redwood-retention-matrix-v1.pdf (single-sheet mapping: store type, retention window, encryption, notes)
- custsec-greenfield-evidence.zip (SOC2 extract, encryption key policy excerpts, sample audit log redaction)

If you'd like, we can provide a signed attestation for procurement that mirrors the above. Ben — can you weigh in on whether we should offer a 30-day backup purge SLA in the draft attestation for this deal?

Emma — quick answers inline and next steps. Quoted your questions below for clarity.

> A) Are snapshots/backups ever copied to a secondary region for DR testing? If yes, which regions?

Short answer: We do not copy customer request/response payload snapshots to secondary regions as part of routine DR testing. Our DR posture for hosted tenants is region-local-first: service recovery efforts attempt to rebuild in-region. In limited planned exercises we may create sanitized recovery artifacts in a DR staging environment; those artifacts are redacted (no full payloads) and any staging copies are constrained to our US DR region (us-east-1) for customers with US tenancy. This behavior is documented in the attached evidence.

> B) Deletion certificate format — timestamped, signed, list of purged artifact IDs?

We provide a machine-generated deletion certificate that includes: deleted-entity identifiers (artifact IDs), deletion timestamps (UTC), and a Redwood signature block (PKI-signed token). We can also include a short human-readable attestation signed by an authorized Redwood officer. We will publish the DocuSign link for the attestation once Ben confirms the wording.

> C) Telemetry access RBAC for short-term telemetry logs

Telemetry containing runtime-sampled identifiers is accessible only via RBAC-protected tooling. Access rules: (1) SRE on-call can view ephemeral traces to diagnose incidents, (2) engineers require ticketed approvals for customer-specific lookups and all such lookups are logged, (3) security & compliance team has broader access for investigations. We enforce least-privilege and require justification for any customer-scoped investigation; these actions are auditable.

Next steps: Ben / Neha — can you review the attestation draft and confirm we can offer the DocuSign attestation with a 30-day backup purge target (we'll mark it as "best-effort 30 days / contractually 90 days unless Dedicated/Private")? Once agreed, I'll push the DocuSign and send the signed attestation back to Emma.

Best,
Jonas
